plan_a_advantages: Increased focus on trail-specific endurance through longer runs.
Incorporation of hill sessions to build climbing strength.
Greater emphasis on recovery with more easy runs.
plan_b_advantages: Includes dedicated speed work (intervals and tempo runs).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it prioritizes building a strong aerobic base and trail-specific endurance through consistent, longer runs at an easy pace. While Plan B includes valuable speed work, it lacks the foundational volume necessary for improving overall running economy and sustained effort – crucial for trail racing. Plan A’s emphasis on longer, controlled runs directly addresses the demands of trail running, while Plan B’s focus on intervals and tempo runs could be detrimental if the athlete isn't already sufficiently conditioned. Furthermore, the inclusion of dedicated hill sessions in Plan A is a key element for trail runners, building the strength and power needed for climbing.
